QUAD 306 POWER AMPLIFIER

Restoring your Quad 306

The 306 is a compact two-channel current-dumping power amplifier, about 50 W per channel into 8 Ω. It runs from roughly ±36–41 V DC rails with 4700 µF reservoir capacitors C10, C11. Both channels are on one motherboard; only the loudspeaker terminals are wired separately.

Status: Draft recap, input/feedback update, zener decoupling, sensitivity option and reservoir capacitors; not user- or bench-tested; no BOM rows physically verified.

You work from three things

  1. Your unitWhat is actually fitted wins. Quad made running changes, and earlier owners may have too.
  2. The documentsQuad's service data and diagrams, and the DADA and community upgrade guides, listed below.
  3. The AI guideAn AI assistant with the Quad Agent skill cross-checks your unit against the documents and says where they disagree.

Safety first

This unit runs from the mains and can hold a dangerous charge after it is unplugged. If you are new to electronics, use this page to plan and to talk to a qualified technician: do not open the case, solder, measure inside or power it up after work yourself. Read the safety guidance.

Start here

  1. Identify it from the outside. Note the serial number and the details in the table below. Photos of the rear label help.
  2. Ask the AI guide. Load the skill into your AI assistant and paste the prompt below. It will ask you questions before giving any values.
  3. Decide the job. A like-for-like recap restores the unit; the optional upgrades change how it behaves. Choose deliberately.
  4. Plan the parts. Use the provisional parts list below and the documents to check it. Have the actual board checked before ordering.
  5. Get the work done safely. Internal work, adjustment and first power-up belong with a competent restorer or qualified technician.

PROMPT FOR YOUR AI ASSISTANT

Read quad-upgrade/SKILL.md and follow it to help me restore my Quad 306. Start by helping me identify it from the outside.

Give the assistant the skill bundle or the whole quad-upgrade folder.
